title: Gardenio — System Health (alert targets)
description: The panels the starter alert pack (BeadsDaemonDown, BridgeDown, dead-man's-switch, involuntary deaths, thread-reply DLQ, trigger starvation, open-PR health) fires on. Every Slack alert's 📊 Graph link deep-links to the panel here that shows the exact signal that fired (ka-0000008039). Panel IDs are stable and referenced by templates/vmalert/configmap.yaml dashboard annotations.

panels.title: What to check first

options.content: **Fleet control-plane health, ordered by blast radius.** Work down: (1) is every component *up* and is the alert pipeline itself alive (a dead vmalert makes every other board look green); (2) are singletons crash-looping; (3) is anything *silently* dropping work — thread-reply DLQ depth, write-failure DROPs, starved triggers; (4) are agents dying on upstream Claude errors, corroborated by the independent status-page leg; (5) the slow leaks — advice context budget, VictoriaLogs retention, OIDC alias freshness. Two legs that disagree mean one of the two is broken — start there.

panels.title: Liveness — is the control plane up?
Component scrape health (up{component})
panels.description: up{} per scraped gardenio component. 1 = scraped-and-healthy, 0 = down, missing line = target absent. Backs BeadsDaemonDown/Absent, BridgeDown/Absent, VMAlertDown.

defaults.noValue: no up{component} series at all — Prometheus is not scraping ANY gardenio component, or the datasource did not answer. This is the most severe empty on the board: it is not “everything down”, it is “we cannot see anything”. Check the VictoriaMetrics datasource first.

panels.title: Beads daemon up
panels.description: up{component="beads"}. 0 for 2m fires BeadsDaemonDown (page) — kbeads down halts ALL orchestration.

defaults.noValue: no up{component="beads"} series — the beads target is not registered for scraping. Distinct from up=0 (target registered, scrape failing): empty means the target vanished from service discovery.

panels.title: Bridges up (slack / jira / gitlab)
panels.description: up{} per bridge. 0 for 5m fires BridgeDown (warn) — bead→Slack, mentions, and JIRA/GitLab ingestion for that bridge stall.

defaults.noValue: no up{component=~"slack-bridge|jira-bridge|gitlab-bridge"} series — no bridge target is registered for scraping. Distinct from up=0 (registered, scrape failing): empty means the targets vanished from service discovery.

panels.title: Alert pipeline (vmalert) up
panels.description: up{component="vmalert"}. 0 for 5m fires VMAlertDown (page). vmalert evaluates every alerting rule — while it is down NO alert can fire, so this is watched by the dead-man's-switch too.

defaults.noValue: no up{component="vmalert"} series — the vmalert target is not registered for scraping, so the alert pipeline is UNMONITORED. Empty is not “alerting is fine”; it is “nothing is checking alerting”.

panels.title: Platform singleton restarts/h (crashloop detector)
panels.description: Container restarts per hour for the long-lived platform singletons (litellm, beads-viewer, the bridges, vmsingle/vtsingle, nats, grafana). Backs PlatformPodCrashLooping (ka-0000003606). Ephemeral agent pods and Job pods (agent/reap/stamp/adopt/migrate) are EXCLUDED so this row shows control-plane crashlooping only — agent churn lives on the Agent reliability row below, and including it here would bury one real singleton crashloop under a dozen agent series. A sustained non-zero line IS a crashloop: check lastState.terminated.reason. reason=OOMKilled means the memory limit sits at or below the real working-set peak — the failure mode that took the litellm proxy (the fleet's LLM data-plane) down ~14% of a day before any alert existed to catch it; compare max_over_time(container_memory_working_set_bytes[7d]) against the container's limit before trimming either.

defaults.noValue: no kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total series for the gardenio namespaces — kube-state-metrics is not reporting, so restarts are UNKNOWN, not zero. A live kube-state-metrics with no restarts draws a flat 0 line.

panels.title: vmalert rule-evaluation freshness (dead-man's-switch)
panels.description: The recording series gardenio:beads_events:rate5m is remote-written by vmalert every evaluation. A gap here = vmalert stopped evaluating → VMAlertNotEvaluating (page). This is the same series absent_over_time() keys on.

defaults.noValue: no gardenio:beads_events:rate5m series — the recording rule is not producing output, which means vmalert is not evaluating rules. That is exactly what this dead-man exists to catch: empty here is the FIRING state, not the healthy one.

panels.title: Agent reliability & delivery
Involuntary deaths per hour, by family
panels.description: Agents killed mid-work (claimed task in flight). increase()/hour by family: context_cancelled (SIGTERM/drain), stop_gate_* (rotation churn). Fires AgentInvoluntaryDeaths (warn). Matches the alert's selection exactly: the coarse context_cancelled_unclaimed completeness family (C9 ka-0000001146) is excluded here as it is from the alert; it lives on the dedicated involuntary-deaths dashboard. Deep dive: the dedicated involuntary-deaths dashboard.

defaults.noValue: gardenio_agent_involuntary_deaths_total returned nothing. The counter does not exist until the first involuntary death, so empty is AMBIGUOUS and this panel cannot resolve it: either no agent has died involuntarily since this controller booted, or the controller is not being scraped. Resolve with up{component="agents"} at the top of this board.

panels.title: Thread-reply DLQ depth, by component
panels.description: gardenio_thread_reply_dlq_depth — Slack thread replies that failed and are stuck in the dead-letter queue. >0 for 10m fires ThreadReplyDLQBacklog (warn): the bot has silently stopped answering some threads. CAVEAT: depth only rises for TRANSIENT failures that enqueue for replay; a deterministic (non-transient) write failure is dropped WITHOUT ever entering the DLQ, so depth can read 0 while replies are silently lost — watch the companion 'write-failure & DROP rate' panel below, not this gauge alone (ka-0000007120).

defaults.noValue: no gardenio_thread_reply_dlq_depth series — the bridges publish this gauge on every replay tick, so empty means the bridges are not reporting, NOT that the DLQ is drained. Check “Bridges up (slack / jira / gitlab)” at the top of this board.

panels.title: Thread-reply write-failure & DROP rate (silent-durability leak)
panels.description: The counters the DLQ-depth gauge above hides. A thread-reply write that fails terminally is DROPPED without ever entering the DLQ when the failure is non-transient (deterministic) — depth stays 0 while replies are silently lost. Watch the shape: a DROP line (esp. reason=nontransient) that tracks the write-failure line 1:1 with a flat enqueued/replayed line means messages are being lost, not queued for replay. Enqueued→replayed is the recovery path (a transient blip that landed later); dropped is permanent loss. Idea N1/N2 from the 2026-07-24 Grafana GRADE (ka-0000007120).

defaults.noValue: none of the four thread-reply durability counters returned data. Each is created on its first write failure, enqueue, replay or drop, so empty is AMBIGUOUS and this panel cannot resolve it: either none has occurred since the bridges booted, or the bridges are not being scraped. Resolve with “Bridges up (slack / jira / gitlab)” on this board — this panel only means something while that reads 1.

panels.title: Starved triggers (should-have-fired but didn't)
panels.description: gardenio_trigger_starved — triggers/gardeners that met their fire condition but haven't fired (cooldown wedged / starved). >0 for 15m fires TriggerStarved (warn). Legend names the trigger bead id.

defaults.noValue: no starved triggers — every trigger with pending work either fired or is inside its own cooldown. Healthy, provided the trigger engine is up (see “Component scrape health” at the top): a dark trigger engine renders the same empty panel.

panels.title: Advice context bytes per archetype vs budget
panels.description: max by (project,role) gardenio_prime_hook_bytes{source="advice"}. Over the 81920-byte hard budget for 30m fires AdviceContextOverBudget (ticket) — the advice corpus regressed and is stealing context from every session in that archetype.

defaults.noValue: no gardenio_prime_hook_bytes{source="advice"} series in this range. This gauge is PUSHED by each agent's own gb prime (POST to vmagent), never scraped from the controller, so empty means no agent primed inside the window — or VMAGENT_URL is unset in the pod spec. Per-archetype advice size is UNKNOWN, not zero bytes.

panels.title: Cold-respawn latency by phase (p95)
panels.description: gardenio_slackbridge_respawn_phase_seconds — thread/DM cold-respawn latency broken down by phase so a multi-minute respawn is attributable to the bridge vs the pod. phase=dispatch = bridge enqueue->spawn decision (bead mint / daemon retries); phase=boot = spawn decision->first proof-of-life (pod schedule + image pull + coop --resume replay + agent ready); phase=total = end-to-end (== gardenio_mention_cold_respawn_seconds). dispatch+boot ≈ total is a built-in cross-check. A phase crossing its anomaly threshold (dispatch>15s / boot>150s / total>180s) bumps gardenio_slackbridge_respawn_phase_slow_total and fires SlackBridgeRespawnPhaseSlow (warn). Origin: ~4-min respawn incident, task ka-0000001457.

defaults.noValue: no gardenio_slackbridge_respawn_phase_seconds_bucket samples in this range — no cold respawn happened in the window, so p95 is UNDEFINED, not fast. Widen the range before reading empty as a pass.

panels.title: Claude upstream outage detector — us (leg A) vs. them (leg B)
Agents failing on upstream Claude errors, by category (leg A — PAGES)
panels.description: sum by (category) (gardenio_agent_upstream_error_active) — live count of agents sitting on an upstream provider error, re-derived every controller sweep. category mirrors coop's error_category enum; category=server_error (HTTP 500/502/503/529, api_error, overloaded) is the leg that PAGES: sum(...{category="server_error"}) > 1 for 10m fires ClaudeUpstreamOutage. READ THIS ALONGSIDE the Claude status-page panel to the right — that adjacency is the whole point: it lets the oncall tell 'us' (status page clean → suspect the LiteLLM proxy, egress, or a credential path) from 'them' (provider corroborates → stop spawning new work; agents self-recover when upstream does).

defaults.noValue: no gardenio_agent_upstream_error_active series. The reporter Reset()s this gauge every sweep and re-publishes only categories with an agent in error, so empty means no agent is failing upstream right now. Healthy — provided the controller is being scraped: corroborate with up{component="agents"} in the scrape-health row and with the Claude status page (leg B) panels below.

panels.title: Claude status page — component severity (leg B — corroborates)
panels.description: max by (component) (gardenio_claude_status_component) rendered as an ordinal severity ladder: 0=operational 1=degraded 2=partial_outage 3=major_outage 4=under_maintenance (-1=unknown fetch fallback). Leg B: the provider's OWN claim about its health, polled from status.claude.com. NEVER pages on its own — a status blip our traffic never touches (claude.ai down while api.anthropic.com is fine) must not wake anyone. claude_api / claude_code are the components our agent traffic depends on; ClaudeStatusPageOutage fires when either sits at partial_outage (>=2) for 5m. When this and the leg-A panel to the left light up together, it's THEM.

defaults.noValue: no gardenio_claude_status_component series — the status poller is not reporting, so leg B is BLIND, not green. Check “Detector liveness — status poller staleness” below before trusting any leg-A/leg-B agreement.

panels.title: Agents failing upstream, by project/role (leg A — who's affected)
panels.description: sum by (project, role) (gardenio_agent_upstream_error_active{category="server_error"}) — the same leg-A server_error signal that PAGES, broken down by project (source) and role so the oncall sees WHICH part of the fleet an outage is hitting. A single project/role dominating points at an isolated credential/proxy path (ours); a broad spread across every project/role is the fingerprint of a provider-wide outage (theirs).

defaults.noValue: no gardenio_agent_upstream_error_active{category="server_error"} series — no agent is currently failing on an upstream 5xx, so blast-radius attribution has nothing to attribute. Healthy only if the controller is being scraped: this Reset-every-sweep gauge renders the same nothing when the reporter is dark. Check up{component="agents"} in the scrape-health row.

panels.title: Upstream-error entries per interval, by category (leg A — edge-triggered)
panels.description: sum by (category) (increase(gardenio_agent_upstream_error_transitions_total[$__rate_interval])) — the edge-triggered count of agents ENTERING an upstream error category, the independent second derivation of the leg-A gauge to its left (advice ka-0000005924: measure every important quantity two ways so the two must agree). A sustained gauge with a flat entries line means the transition detector is broken; a climbing entries line with a near-zero gauge means agents are entering AND recovering quickly (healthy churn, not an outage).

defaults.noValue: no gardenio_agent_upstream_error_transitions_total series — no agent has ENTERED an upstream error category since this controller booted. Healthy; the counter is created on first entry.

panels.title: Upstream-outage deaths per hour, by project/role (post-mortem attribution)
panels.description: sum by (project, role) (increase(gardenio_agent_involuntary_deaths_total{family="upstream_api_error"}[1h])) — agents that actually DIED to an upstream Claude error, the honest post-mortem 'what killed the fleet today' view broken down by project (source) and role. Complementary to leg A: leg A counts agents LIVE-erroring right now (detection, what pages); this counts terminal deaths after the damage (attribution). Populates once the upstream_api_error death family lands (ka-0000000202); reads empty until then, which is correct.

defaults.noValue: no gardenio_agent_involuntary_deaths_total{family="upstream_api_error"} series — no agent has died to an upstream outage since this controller booted. Healthy; there is nothing to attribute.

panels.title: Claude status page — open incidents by impact (leg B)
panels.description: sum by (impact) (gardenio_claude_status_open_incidents) — count of unresolved status.claude.com incidents by impact (none/minor/major/critical). Corroborating context for the leg-A page. Note an incident stays open through Statuspage's 'monitoring' window well after service is restored, so a lingering count here is expected in an outage tail and is NOT on its own a reason to keep holding spawns.

defaults.noValue: no gardenio_claude_status_open_incidents series — the status poller is not reporting, so open-incident count is UNKNOWN, not zero. A live poller with no incidents draws a flat 0 line; check the poller-staleness deadman below.

panels.title: Detector liveness — status poller staleness (deadman)
panels.description: time() - gardenio_claude_status_last_check_timestamp_seconds — seconds since the leg-B poller's last SUCCESSFUL fetch. ClaudeStatusPollerStale fires when the indicator is absent OR this exceeds 600s (10 missed 60s polls) for 15m: leg B has gone blind and a firing ClaudeUpstreamOutage can no longer self-diagnose us-vs-them. A healthy poller hugs zero and saws up to ~60s between polls; a line climbing past the red 600s line means the poller is wedged or its egress to status.claude.com is broken (the poller is disabled outright when GARDENIO_CLAUDE_STATUS_POLL_INTERVAL=0).

defaults.noValue: no gardenio_claude_status_last_check_timestamp_seconds series — the deadman itself has nothing to measure, which is worse than a large staleness value: the poller has never checked in since this controller booted. Leg B is unusable until this populates.

panels.title: Detector liveness — poll errors & overall indicator (leg B health)
panels.description: The two remaining leg-B health signals. poll error rate = sum(rate(gardenio_claude_status_check_errors_total[$__rate_interval])): fetch/parse failures against status.claude.com — on failure the poller leaves prior gauges STALE rather than zeroing them (writing 'all operational' on a failed fetch would let a partition actively suppress the outage alert), so a rising error rate is what precedes the staleness deadman to its left. overall indicator = gardenio_claude_status_indicator on the ordinal ladder 0=none 1=minor 2=major 3=critical (the page-wide roll-up, distinct from the per-component severity in the state-timeline above).

defaults.noValue: neither gardenio_claude_status_check_errors_total nor gardenio_claude_status_indicator exists — the status poller has not run since boot. Empty is NOT “zero poll errors”: it means leg B never started.

panels.title: VictoriaLogs disk usage vs cap (retention self-trim)
panels.description: On-disk bytes for gardenio-victoria-logs (vl_data_size_bytes, storage+indexdb) as a fraction of its -retention.maxDiskSpaceUsageBytes cap (vl_max_disk_space_usage_bytes). VictoriaLogs enforces min(retentionPeriod=30d, disk cap): past the cap it self-trims the OLDEST partitions regardless of the 30d window, so a rising line means effective retention is silently dropping below 30d. Backs VlsingleDiskUsageHigh (ka-0000001302); the red threshold marks the 0.75 alert point. Requires vlsingle.metrics.scrape (the vl_* series only reach vmsingle when the store self-scrapes).

defaults.noValue: no vl_data_size_bytes / vl_max_disk_space_usage_bytes series for vlsingle — VictoriaLogs is not being scraped, so disk headroom is UNKNOWN, not zero. Note the expr also drops the ratio when the cap gauge is 0 (cap unset), which renders empty rather than dividing by zero.

panels.title: Attribution integrity — can each bridge attribute inbound events to a human?
OIDC operator-alias coverage by bridge component
panels.description: gardenio_bridge_slack_oidc_alias_coverage{component} — size of the operator→Slack alias map each bridge holds. A bridge at 0 cannot attribute its inbound events (GitLab MRs, Jira mentions, trigger fires) to a human operator, so that traffic lands unattributed. Live 2026-08-25: slack-bridge=30 but gitlab-bridge / jira-bridge / trigger-engine all sit at 0 — a real operator-attribution blind spot. Whether the non-slack bridges SHOULD hold aliases is a product question; if 0 is expected the red tile still proves it rather than leaving it invisible. Verified against gardenio-vmsingle (ka-0000006408).

defaults.noValue: no gardenio_bridge_slack_oidc_alias_coverage series — no bridge is publishing alias coverage, so attribution integrity is UNKNOWN, not 0%. Check “Bridges up (slack / jira / gitlab)” at the top of this board.

panels.title: OIDC alias resync freshness by bridge component
panels.description: time() - gardenio_bridge_slack_oidc_resync_last_success_timestamp_seconds{component}: age of each bridge's last SUCCESSFUL operator-alias resync. A rising line means the resync loop has stalled and alias coverage is decaying (a stalled resync is why the coverage panel above drops to 0). Bridges that have NEVER resynced report timestamp 0; the `> 0` filter drops them here (their zero coverage already shows in the panel to the left) so the axis reflects only bridges that do resync. yellow >30m, red >1h. Verified against gardenio-vmsingle (ka-0000006408).

defaults.noValue: no successful OIDC alias resync has ever been recorded (the expr drops the series when the last-success timestamp is 0), so freshness is UNKNOWN. Empty here means the resync has never succeeded — it is a finding, not a clean bill of health.

panels.title: Open PRs — is anything waiting with no owner?
Open PRs into main, by state (PR sweeper's hourly count)
panels.description: The PR sweeper's last hourly count of open PRs into main (gardenio_open_prs, plan gd-3F4W22h2nT step 10). open is every open PR; desk_queue the ones an open merge escalation names, so the merge desk will see them; orphaned the ones with no merge escalation and no living owner when the sweeper found them, before it escalated or closed them. Orphans should stay near zero: gb stop's PR park and the kd close guard leave the sweeper nothing to find. Backs OpenPROrphansHigh; the red line is its threshold (5). The Slack Agent Dashboard carries the same figures as its open-PR line.

defaults.noValue: no gardenio_open_prs series: the PR sweeper (trigger gd-7cQvwrgva9, docs/pr-sweeper.md) has not recorded a run since the controller started, or it is disabled. The open-PR count is UNKNOWN, not zero.

panels.title: Oldest open PR and oldest orphan (hours)
panels.description: Age in hours, from createdAt, of the oldest open PR the sweeper considers (desk train/revert PRs and human PRs excluded) and of the oldest orphan (0 with none), at the PR sweeper's last run (gardenio_open_pr_oldest_age_hours). The merge desk merges or sends back within hours, so a PR past two days is stuck: an un-reworked send-back, a PR the desk keeps returning, or a draft. Backs OpenPROldestOverdue; the red line is its threshold (48h). The record's oldest_open_pr names the PR.

defaults.noValue: no gardenio_open_prs series: the PR sweeper (trigger gd-7cQvwrgva9, docs/pr-sweeper.md) has not recorded a run since the controller started, or it is disabled. The open-PR count is UNKNOWN, not zero.

panels.title: Merge train
panels.description: The merge desk's train at the PR sweeper's last run (gardenio_merge_train_state): none (no open merge-train PR), pending (checks running), green, red, conflicting, or revert (a merge-train-revert PR is open, so the desk merges nothing else). Red, conflicting and revert stop the desk's batched merges.

defaults.noValue: no gardenio_open_prs series: the PR sweeper (trigger gd-7cQvwrgva9, docs/pr-sweeper.md) has not recorded a run since the controller started, or it is disabled. The open-PR count is UNKNOWN, not zero.

panels.title: Hours since the PR sweeper's last count
panels.description: How old the figures on this row are: hours since the PR sweeper last recorded its count (gardenio_open_pr_health_timestamp_seconds). It records hourly. Backs OpenPRHealthStale (red at 4h): past that, the sweeper is disabled, unsealed, or dying before its last step, and the two panels above are frozen.

defaults.noValue: no gardenio_open_prs series: the PR sweeper (trigger gd-7cQvwrgva9, docs/pr-sweeper.md) has not recorded a run since the controller started, or it is disabled. The open-PR count is UNKNOWN, not zero.
